title: Machine-learning and expert co-screening identifies two new silver-catalyzed cycloadditions
summary: Researchers at the Zelinsky Institute used unsupervised machine learning to filter and cluster candidate atom-economic cycloaddition reactions generated from quantum-chemical data, then used a digital co-expert and chemist review to prioritize experiments. The team experimentally confirmed two previously undescribed silver-catalyzed cycloaddition reactions yielding new products within about one week.
ai_technology: Machine-learning candidate filtering and clustering combined with the digital co-expert reaction-prioritization workflow
organization: N. D. Zelinsky Institute of Organic Chemistry, Russian Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: Researchers at the Zelinsky Institute used unsupervised machine learning to filter and cluster candidate atom-economic cycloaddition reactions generated from quantum-chemical data, then used a digital co-expert and chemist review to prioritize experiments.
evidence.unknown: Two reactions were confirmed from a heavily filtered set of computational candidates, with final selection and validation by chemists. The reported approximately 180-fold acceleration is a comparison for the expert-screening bottleneck, not a general chemical-discovery speedup. The abstract does not specify individual products or reaction yields; no such details are inferred here.
evidence.ai_role: Unsupervised ML filtered and clustered computationally generated reaction candidates to reduce the set for review; the digital co-expert helped prioritize candidates. Human chemists made the final selection and performed experimental validation. The source reports two newly confirmed cycloadditions; the system was a human-AI pipeline, not autonomous discovery.
